svg.title: Why the encoded future changes an eviction
svg.desc: A teaching cache with one set and two ways contains property lines A and B after semantic request nineteen. A was touched at eighteen and is needed at twenty; B was touched at nineteen and is needed at twenty-three. Scale6 deadlines twenty-one and twenty-six give remaining distances two and seven, hence victim scores zero and one. LRU evicts A for an incoming scores line C; ECG evicts B. This is a worked algorithm example, not measured benchmark performance.
svg.text: Why the encoded future changes an eviction
A recent line is not necessarily the line needed soonest. The same graph gives a concrete counterexample.
Same access: u=8 | CSR j=18 | request s=19 | property v=18 | line B
teaching set 0: two resident property ways
The score is distanceRRPV(remaining) = min(7, floor(log2(remaining)) / 2), rounded down.
Full14 yields tighter deadlines 20 and 23 for these two accesses, with the same score ordering.
the same new scores-line C needs a way
Oldest touch: A at 18 -> evict A
Largest score: B at 1 -> evict B
Next request p[7] at s20: miss
Next request p[7] at s20: hit
Only the replacement choice differs. The graph, p[18] = 1/128, and dirty-data handling remain unchanged.
GET FRESH KNOWLEDGE TO THE LLC
private hits still need a metadata route
Native line payload: D=32. Full14's default model uses D=21.
General victim order: DEAD, non-property, then scored properties. Unknown uses max(RRPV, local GRASP).
